# Revised Candidate Approach — product-1 quest (TELOS v0.3.0 / PYLAE Gate v1)

Branched from `main @ fc0fa05`. Governing pre-review: `docs/institutional-memory/iliad/PRE-REVIEWS/2026-08-27-product-1.json`. This approach is the Daedalus workshop input; convergence is submission, not authorization. The frozen Production-Readiness Master Checklist and v0.2.0 review findings remain unchanged and governing.

## 1. Objective and boundary

Close all 10 release blockers and 7 governance corrections; freeze the Phase-0 product contract; deliver Phase-1a distribution; repair the normative authority chain; and release PYLAE Gate v1 as v0.3.0 only from the exact qualified and Eye-accepted commit.

Per the recorded S0 rulings, v1 is a local single-user CLI. Identity, multi-tenancy, and clustered runtime are out of scope through signed ADR PD-001. This boundary is enforced by both a tracked-source no-listener oracle and runtime command tests that deny Node network-listener primitives while exercising every CLI command. The flagship remains a demonstration/evidence viewer and future operator-console candidate, not a production console or this round's deployed Pages payload.

Phase 1b items remain in the readiness register with owners and target rounds: durable crash-consistent state, authenticated-principal authority binding, Auth0-over-OIDC service identity, key rotation, backup/restore, and supported sandbox documentation. The governing identifiers are `product-1-ruling-identity-provider` and `product-1-ruling-oauth-seat-transport`.

## 2. Enforcement-changing specifications

Every E1–E6 change requires signed required-seat review and at least one regression that reproduces the original defect.

### E1 — Hestia merge attestation

`workflows/hestia.js` will stop treating model prose as merge evidence. Before any model process starts, the deterministic controller records the repository set, run identifier, start time, and a unique branch namespace such as `pylae-run/<run-id>/`. Model processes receive no GitHub token or other repository-mutation credential. They return patches and structured proposals only. The controller is the sole process allowed to push branches, create/update PRs, or call the merge endpoint; it records every attempted operation before executing it.

For each proposed PR, the controller parses `pr_url` into `{owner,repo,number}`, rejects foreign or malformed URLs, captures the 40-hex head SHA, and merges through `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/merge` with the expected `sha`. A head-moved response is final for that attempt and is never retried with a newly fetched head.

The in-workflow read-only verifier and field-by-field gate retain distinct fail-closed outcomes for missing verification, blocked shipment, absent merge confirmation, merged despite blocked, foreign repository, head mismatch, and merge-SHA mismatch. Its `merged[]` field is explicitly advisory.

The authoritative `workflows/tools/attest-merges.mjs` independently queries GitHub. It paginates every open and closed PR in the recorded repositories and selects every head ref in the controller-created namespace; it also verifies every PR number and branch recorded in the controller's operation ledger. Because model processes cannot create arbitrary remote refs or PRs, this namespace plus controller ledger is the complete attempt surface rather than an inference from model output or a broad time window. Missing pages, API errors, an unexpected controller mutation, a namespaced PR absent from the workflow report, or any merged PR not certified as confirmed produces exit 2. The attestation contains direct API observations for PR identity, head, merged state, and merge commit.

Acceptance includes eight adversarial workflow fixtures; a colluding ship/verifier fixture contradicted by stubbed GitHub truth; omitted namespaced PR detection; pagination coverage; head movement; unrelated concurrent PR activity that does not create a false positive; and a clean authoritative attestation. Workflows CI runs both suites.

### E2 — ai-native-memory freshness and authority-anchored sources

`ai-native-memory/scripts/gate.mjs` extracts byte-stable freshness logic into `scripts/lib/freshness.mjs` and re-derives every query's `expected` value from `derived_from` at gate time. Missing, dangling, stale, escaping, symlinked, or unanchored inputs are denied with distinct reason codes.

A source is admissible only when it is content-addressed with a recomputed address equal to its identifier and is reachable from the hash-pinned authority map or contract set governed by `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json`.

The trust-chain head is supplied outside the candidate tree. `--trust-anchor <commit>` or `PYLAE_TRUST_ANCHOR` remains mandatory, but CI must not derive it from an untrusted PR/head SHA:

- Repository CI reads the accepted authority commit from a protected environment variable maintained by the Eye/release authority and unavailable to PR tokens. Pull-request checks remain anchored to that accepted commit; proposed authority changes cannot grant themselves authority before acceptance.
- After an authority-changing commit is accepted on protected `main`, the authority holder updates the protected anchor as a separate controlled action. Only subsequent runs may treat that commit as the trust root.
- Release requires the signed tag target to equal this externally stored accepted commit.
- Local use requires an explicit operator-selected commit or a verified signed tag; the result records which trust decision was supplied and never silently substitutes `HEAD`.

The gate resolves `CURRENT-AUTHORITY.json` and every admissible source from the anchored Git object graph using `git cat-file`. Working-tree divergence produces `anchor-mismatch`; an absent or unresolvable external anchor produces `anchor-unavailable`. A PR that rewrites source, expected answer, and in-tree authority together therefore remains denied because it cannot alter the protected external anchor.

Acceptance includes fixed-anchor full-lockstep mutation, source-only staleness, unanchored source, missing anchor, path escape, symlink escape, pull-request head substitution, and protected-anchor dogfood cases.

### E3 — auditor full taxonomy and no-clean-on-zero

`ai-native-memory/scripts/audit.mjs` recognizes a directly supplied memory root through its marker predicate, returns exit 2 on zero discovered sets unless `--allow-empty` is explicit, and validates all eight record kinds through `RECORD_SET_LAYOUT`. Markdown decisions use front-matter enums only, preserving the bytes of AM-40, AM-41, and AM-42.

The legacy atropos/lachesis cycle-1 decisions are superseded by new content-addressed records without an allowlist. Dogfood must be green after the in-plugin content repair, and the PR body enumerates every newly exposed failure.

### E4 — production gate default flip

After parsing the `signed` flag, `build-gate/gate.mjs` enforces:

- production plus unsigned is a blocker;
- production plus `allow_unsigned` is a blocker;
- unsigned without explicit `allow_unsigned` is a blocker;
- signed plus `allow_unsigned` is a contradiction blocker.

`headline_checks` includes profile and unsigned-opt-in state. The nine unset-trust-mode fixtures and two advisory examples explicitly opt in; production unsigned blocks; production signed passes; gate and stress suites stay green.

### E5 — authority-chain repair

Create content-addressed NORMATIVE-CURRENT successors to `Multi-Model Agentic Build Gate` and `Claude-Led Multi-Model Prototype Workflow`. The first is reconciled to current paths, signed-by-default behavior, provider provenance, Iliad lifecycle, and the PYLAE v1 boundary. The second is explicitly limited to prototype planning, capability acquisition, dynamic council, and market-readiness, with code-enforced and advisory claims separated.

Preserve both draft files byte-identically as historical provenance. Mark `Claude-Grok-Agy Hierarchical Agentic Workflow` historical/superseded, preserve its bytes, and redirect every governing citation. A new normative invariant requires every current governing citation to terminate in a reviewed content-addressed NORMATIVE-CURRENT record; historical references are accepted only when explicitly typed non-governing provenance.

`verify-contracts.mjs` fails when a current normative record treats a draft or historical artifact as authority. All root invariants, loadout contracts, capability packets, comprehension queries, and required-doc citations are redirected and verified.

### E6 — enrollment uniqueness, root sweep, zero dependencies, and discriminating oracles

`verify-contracts.mjs` enforces uniqueness across enrollment roots, authorizations, and `enrollment_run` identifiers with bijective cardinality checks; performs an explicit root `INVARIANTS.json` sweep; and enforces the revised zero-runtime-dependency invariant over every tracked package manifest, including machine-readable exceptions for the flagship.

Every NORMATIVE record receives structured `oracle.executable` metadata. The new `run-oracles.mjs` executes file and npm-script oracles under timeouts and validates content-addressed evidence directories. Missing, unrunnable, failing, timing-out, or empty evidence produces distinct failures.

Negative discrimination cannot be implemented as an alternate flag, alternate script, or hard-coded self-test branch. Each executable declaration identifies its governed input closure and a deterministic mutation recipe. The runner creates an isolated temporary copy, runs the production command on the clean copy, applies the declared violating mutation, and reruns the exact same executable, script, arguments, and code path, changing only the declared root/cwd placeholder. The mutated run must exit nonzero with an allowed invariant-specific reason. The runner rejects command drift between positive and negative executions. Evidence-directory checks similarly remove or corrupt a declared record and rerun the same production validator.

Acceptance includes: a genuine oracle failure; timeout; a constant-success oracle; a program that merely exits nonzero on `--self-check-negative`; an npm script whose alternate negative script fails but whose production script ignores the mutation; and a correctly discriminating same-path mutation. The full backfill and both verification tools run in institutional-memory CI.

## 3. Governance ceremony

One live TELOS re-authorization run at `docs/runs/product-authorization-1/`, build ID `iliad-product-1-authz`, with signed claude/agy/codex seats and advisory grok/gemini seats, authorizes both the AM-42 enrollment-flip regularization and AM-43's classification of `cli/` and `connectors/meta-ads-mcp/` into `PACKAGE_ROOTS_EXCLUDE`.

AM-43 is a new decision with one fenced JSON block. AM-42 remains byte-identical. Mutable registry surfaces record AM-43's amendment and retroactive ratification; AM-43 and the deviation record pin AM-42's SHA-256. New pinned documents use the write-then-hash-then-pin sequence. The eight coordinated surfaces—inventory and re-weave, frozen inventory tests, comprehension expectations, Iliad deferred list, repository-manifest products/counts, and section 5c ruling generalization—land together.

Acceptance requires an AUTHORIZED summary plus green enrollment, uniqueness, and deferred-equality checks.

## 4. Product contract, naming, CLI, and Meta Ads

Register PYLAE through the governed mythological-vocabulary lifecycle or an approved product-brand carve-out before using it normatively. Operator-facing surfaces translate mythological roles through `docs/institutional-memory/product/GLOSSARY.md`.

Create `docs/institutional-memory/product/` with PD-001 through PD-007 covering product form/user, boundary, flagship role, state model, topology, naming/versioning/publishing, and role glossary. Add `production-readiness.json` with owner, priority, phase, status, signed ADR reference and hash, evidence, and target round for every checklist item. N/A requires a signed ADR. A deterministic renderer maintains `docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS.md`.

The register defines hard automatic no-go conditions now. The v0.3.0 workflow runs a Phase-1a release profile and cannot claim GA. A future GA profile is already fail-closed on every unresolved P0 item and cannot be changed to reporting-only by a command-line flag. `render-readiness.mjs --check` and product verification test the profile rules and planted unresolved-P0 cases.

Add `product-version.json`; rename `v4-build-gate`, `v4-forge`, and `v4-breakout` packages to `telos-*`; align all package and plugin versions at 0.3.0; retain the verifier-pinned `narcissus-flagship` name; and do not add a root package manifest.

A tracked-doc and manifest oracle rejects Node runtime claims below 22.12.0 outside frozen run evidence. It covers the enumerated current offenders and a planted `Node 18+` fixture.

The private zero-runtime-dependency `cli/` package exposes `pylae init`, `doctor`, `version`, and `verify`. Commands resolve helpers relative to the installation root, never cwd. `doctor` checks Node 22.12+, mode-specific provenance, bwrap, required environment, and Ed25519 support. `verify` aggregates `verify-contracts`, committed self-weave, and fail-closed demo checks. Static tracked-source inspection plus runtime-denied network primitives enforce the local no-listener boundary.

Meta Ads governance adds a private package and manifest/CI coverage. Caps must match `^[0-9]{1,6}$`, be safe positive integers, and remain below a frozen hard ceiling. Budget arguments and closed ID/kind grammars are validated before environment or token access. `META_ADS_ENABLED` is a startup kill switch. Hermetic tests, `HUMAN-SETUP.md`, and the `env-surface.json` scanned-directory extension cover all five `META_*` names.

## 5. Installation and source-release integrity

The installable v1 product is the complete source-release bundle, not the standalone `npm pack cli` component. The component README states that it requires the source tree. PD-006 records extraction or tag checkout plus Node 22.12+ as the supported installation contract.

The release builder stages the exact qualified commit using `git archive`, then adds generated metadata without calling the result a byte-identical Git tree:

- `RELEASE-IDENTITY.json` records tag, commit SHA, Git tree SHA, product version, and release-workflow source.
- `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` records every staged path, file type, executable mode, and SHA-256, including `RELEASE-IDENTITY.json`; generated manifest files are explicitly separated from the Git-tree payload.
- The builder independently reconstructs the Git blob/tree object hashes for the archived tracked payload and requires the reconstructed root to equal the recorded Git tree SHA.
- The complete final archive is covered by `SHA256SUMS` and GitHub build-provenance attestation. The bundle does not claim that internally editable metadata authenticates itself.

The source bundle is built twice in clean temporary staging directories with normalized order, ownership, modes, and timestamps; byte inequality aborts the release.

Checkout mode requires `.git`, checks full history, reports live HEAD, and cross-checks any release identity. Archive mode requires the identity and source manifest, verifies all manifest entries, rejects missing and extra payload files, reconstructs the Git tree, and reports embedded provenance. Neither mode fails open. With neither Git metadata nor release identity, doctor returns `unprovenanced-install`.

Offline doctor/verify proves bundle consistency, not publisher authenticity, and reports signature/attestation verification as not performed offline. Installation documentation requires verification of the published checksum and provenance attestation before extraction. Online `pylae verify` verifies the release attestation. A one-file identity tamper fails the manifest check; coordinated identity/manifest/archive tampering fails the external checksum or attestation test.

The clean-room job extracts only the final artifact into an empty directory outside a checkout, verifies the published artifact first, then runs doctor, version, and `verify --offline-checks`. Missing helpers, extra files, identity mutation, payload mutation, and unprovenanced extraction all fail.

## 6. Freshness, release, deployment, review workflow, and flagship

`run.mjs --exact-head` requires live HEAD equality, clean worktree, and a complete `source_ref` sweep, with distinct fatal codes and always-emitted freshness/equality fields. Release runs exact-head; CI wording does not equate a green record with reality.

`release.yml` is fail-closed:

1. The tag must be annotated and signed. Verification uses a fresh isolated keyring containing only the committed release public key, but that key is accepted only after its fingerprint equals an expected fingerprint stored in a protected release environment outside the tagged tree. The tag target must equal the externally stored Eye-accepted trust-anchor commit. Unknown, unsigned, wrong-key, unverifiable, or self-substituted keys abort. Required check runs are matched by expected workflow/check identity and trusted GitHub App, not name alone.
2. The complete source bundle and CLI component are built twice and byte-compared; checksums, Syft SBOMs, and provenance attestations are produced for each published payload.
3. A literal closed filename allowlist is compared exactly against release assets. Missing or extra assets fail. `gh attestation verify` runs against every payload before the release is marked usable.

`RELEASING.md` documents the out-of-tree fingerprint prerequisite, protected environment, immutable-tag setting, signing ceremony, correction process, and the v0.2.0 4,558-to-4,559 correction.

Pages CI uploads `demo-${github.sha}` only after required main-push CI. The `workflow_run` deploy requires success, push event, and main head branch; downloads solely from the triggering run ID; and checks the embedded SHA against `head_sha`. PR and non-main fixtures cannot deploy. The payload remains `demo/`; flagship deployment stays registered for a later round.

The review workflow uses an owner-controlled SHA-pinned plugin fork. Plugin code runs only in a contents-read job with neither PR-write nor OIDC permission. Its OAuth model credential exposure is documented as residual model-spend risk. A separate deterministic post job, containing no marketplace/plugin execution and no model credential, downloads a bounded schema-validated artifact and posts via `gh api`. Workflow lint rejects write/OIDC in the review job and plugin execution in the post job.

Flagship work adds an ErrorBoundary around lazy WebGL with an operable DOM fallback; a 375x667 regression with no document-level horizontal overflow and usable stage scrolling; accessible tabs with roving focus and arrow navigation; WCAG 2 A/AA axe checks across both views/themes; malformed-base64 fail-closed behavior; all OFL-1.1 texts; and third-party notices. Each enforcement change has its own regression. CODEOWNERS remains a named-owner register item because the project currently has one maintainer.

## 7. Slice order and validation

Slices are: freshness; plugin self-containment; E2; E3; E1; E6; E4; product records/ADRs; naming/version alignment; combined authorization ceremony with AM-43, CLI, Meta Ads, and coordinated pins; release/Pages/review workflow; flagship/demo/fonts; E5 authority repair; and train-end full re-weave.

Authority-changing slices are tested under the previously accepted external anchor and cannot self-authorize. After Eye acceptance, the protected anchor is advanced as a separate governance action before downstream gate claims depend on the new record set.

Each slice runs its package-defined suites, `verify-contracts`, applicable oracle execution, review, Eye acceptance, and Argo ledger recording. No slice claims committed weave freshness until the train-end republication regenerates and pins all woven outputs at the final head.

## 8. Quest-level acceptance and non-claims

Required evidence includes a pre-implementation comprehension-gate GRANTED artifact; signed reviews for E1–E6 and the ceremony; merge-anchored step-ledger entries; green package suites; green contract and oracle verification; final committed self-weave at exact head; the authorized combined council summary; complete normative citation closure; product-subsystem enrollment; a product-1 retrospective with feed-forward landing sites; and release execution at the exact externally anchored, Eye-accepted commit.

PYLAE Gate v0.3.0 is explicitly a Phase-1a local single-user release, not GA, SaaS, a network service, or a production operator console. Offline bundle checks establish consistency, not publisher authenticity. Model councils provide reviewed evidence but never production authority. The Eye and deterministic gates remain the authority boundary; the self-weave verifier remains governed by CI/review rather than falsely described as independently pinned.
